'''''Convolvulus tricolor''''' (syn. ''C. minor'') is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[family (botany)|family]] [[Convolvulaceae]], [[native species|native]] to [[Mediterranean Europe]]. Common names include '''dwarf morning-glory''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=COTR17|taxon=Convolvulus tricolor|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> '''tricolour convolvulus''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and ''belle de jour''.

== Description ==
It is a short to medium annual plant with solitary long-stalked flowers. The flower is a tri-coloured funnel-shaped bloom about three centimeters wide, blue with white and a yellow centre.{{Cn|date=May 2023}}

== Taxonomy ==

=== Synonyms ===
* ''Convolvulus maroccanus''  [[Batt.]]
* ''Convolvulus meonanthus'' [[Hoffmanns.]] & [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link|Link]]
* ''Convolvulus minor'' 
* ''Convolvulus pseudotricolor'' [[Bertol.]]

=== Subspecies ===
* ''Convolvulus tricolor'' subsp. ''hortensis'' ([[Batt.]]) [[René Maire|Maire]]
* ''Convolvulus tricolor'' subsp. ''meonanthus'' ([[Hoffmanns.]] & [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link|Link]]) [[René Maire|Maire]] 
* ''Convolvulus tricolor'' subsp. ''pentapetaloides'' ([[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]) [[O.Bolòs]] & [[Vigo]] 
* ''Convolvulus tricolor'' subsp. ''tricolor'' [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]<ref name = RJB>[http://www.anthos.es/v22/index.php?set_locale=es Convolvulus tricolor] [[Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid|Real Jardín Botánico]]: [[Proyecto Anthos]]</ref>

[[O. Bolòs]] et [[J. Vigoe]] distinguish ''Convolvulus tricolor'' ssp. ''pentapetaloides'' ([[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]) O.Bolòs & Vigo, found in the Balearic isles, from the type subspecies (''Convolvulus tricolor ssp tricolor'') by flowers that are smaller (7–10 mm), and both the [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] and the [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]] having few or no hairs.<ref name=herbario/>

== Habitat ==
Common on cultivated land, dry open habitats, sandy places and roadsides.{{Cn|date=May 2023}}

== Distribution ==
This flowering plant is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Mediterranean Basin]], particularly the south, but it is occasionally seen in other areas of similar climate. In Spain it can be found in the [[Balearic Islands]],<ref name=herbario>[http://herbarivirtual.uib.es/cas-med/especie/5389.html Herbario Virtual: Convolvulus tricolor L. subsp. pentapetaloides]</ref>
and [[Andalusia]], especially in the [[Costa del Sol]].<ref>García Guardia, G. (1988). Flores Silvestres de Andalucía. Alcorcón:Rueda. {{ISBN|84-7207-049-2}}.</ref>

== Cultivation ==
''Convolvulus tricolor'' is usually cultivated for ornamental purposes. The species<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/105536/Convolvulus-tricolor/Details | title = ''Convolvulus tricolor'' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 12 April 2020}}</ref> and the [[cultivar]] 'Blue Ensign'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/106101/Convolvulus-tricolor-Blue-Ensign/Details | title = ''Convolvulus tricolor'' 'Blue Ensign' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 12 April 2020}}</ref> have both received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].
